newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ dollar trades narrow range, closes on lows.
newsitem.headline: NZ dollar trades narrow range, closes on lows.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar closed on its lows after trading a narrow range on Monday.
Dealers said there was no real offshore interest and interbank flows were subdued, with players taking a cautious line before Thursday's economic projections from the Reserve Bank of New Zealand.
A slightly weaker Australian dollar was also weighing on the Kiwi, which finished at US$0.7015/22 and 68.91 on its Trade-Weighted Index, down from 0.7036/43 and 69.16 at the opening.
Dealers said they expected a "steady as she goes" statement from the central bank and there was a general feeling that monetary conditions were tight enough.

"Right now people pretty much think if anything it may have gone over the top a little bit," said a Wellington dealer. He noted the TWI had climbed from around 68.20 at the end of last month, while 90-day rates had risen to 7.6 percent from 7.45.
One dealer predicted a 0.7005-30 range overnight, while another saw 0.7000-40.
